record.original_question: Is the geodesic flow of a metric of non-positive curvature on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure?

evidence.quote: Is the geodesic flow of a metric of non-positive curvature on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $\rho$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $S$ whose sectional (Gaussian) curvature satisfies $K \leq 0$ everywhere. Let $T^1 S$ denote the unit tangent bundle of $(S,\rho)$, and let $\varphi_t : T^1 S \to T^1 S$ denote the geodesic flow. Equip $T^1 S$ with the Liouville measure $\mu$ (the smooth invariant probability measure induced by the Sasaki metric, or equivalently the product of the Riemannian area on $S$ with the normalized arclength on each fiber circle).

Question: Must the geodesic flow $\varphi_t$ be ergodic with respect to $\mu$? That is, is it true that for every Borel set $A \subseteq T^1 S$ with $\varphi_t(A) = A$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, one has $\mu(A) \in \{0, 1\}$?
artifact.category_tag: geodesic flows on nonpositively curved surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as open. Ergodicity is classical in the strictly negatively curved case (Hopf, Anosov), but in nonpositive curvature the presence of "flat" geodesics obstructs the standard arguments. Partial results (e.g., Burns–Gelfert, and ergodicity under the assumption that the set of points of negative curvature has finitely many connected components, due to Brin–Burago and subsequent work) are known, but the general genus $\geq 2$ case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the ergodicity of geodesic flows on surfaces of nonpositive curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Ergodicity of the geodesic flow with respect to Liouville measure proven under the assumption that the set of points with negative curvature has finitely many connected components.
status_evidence.claim: General ergodicity in nonpositive curvature is not established; only conditional results are known.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists ergodicity of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open in a standard problem collection on geodesic flows.
